title: AI performance coach: agent with tools over services, structured memory, proposals vs committed changes, chat UI
steps:
AGENT CORE (PRD §4, §6, §12, §14; docs/agent-architecture.md from M1; milestones M5). BEFORE writing any agent code, invoke the `claude-api` skill (Skill tool) and read its TypeScript README, tool-use.md and streaming.md plus shared/tool-use-concepts.md and shared/prompt-caching.md; follow them over memory. Facts to respect (from that skill): default model id `claude-opus-5-5` (exact string, no date suffix); thinking is always on — omit `thinking` or send `{type: "adaptive"}`, never `disabled`/`budget_tokens`; set `output_config.effort` explicitly (default is `medium`; use `medium` for chat turns, `high` for program/cycle generation proposals); forced `tool_choice` any/tool returns 400 — use `auto` and steer in the prompt with `strict: true` tool schemas; no assistant prefill; check `stop_reason` (`refusal` with `stop_details`, `max_tokens`, `pause_turn`) before reading content; include server-side refusal fallbacks by default (`client.beta.messages` with `betas: ["server-side-fallback-2026-07-01"]` and `fallbacks: "default"`); stream long responses; when streaming with client tools set `eager_input_streaming: true` and validate every parsed tool input against its zod schema before executing; return all tool_result blocks for a turn in one user message; `is_error: true` for failed tools; typed SDK errors (Anthropic.RateLimitError etc.), SDK types for messages/tools.

Build src/lib/server/agent/:
- `LlmProvider` interface with two implementations: `AnthropicProvider` (@anthropic-ai/sdk, server-only, key from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY via the zod env — never imported by client code) and `MockProvider` (deterministic, scriptable: given a conversation it emits scripted tool calls/text so every agent path is testable offline). Provider chosen by env (COACH_PROVIDER=anthropic|mock; mock in dev/test/CI by default; anthropic required in production when the key exists — fail closed with a clear coach-unavailable state otherwise).
- Tools as typed definitions (zod input schemas → JSON schema with additionalProperties:false, strict) that call the SAME services the UI uses (M2–M4), grouped: history (get_training_history, get_exercise_history, get_running_history, get_recent_workouts, get_personal_records), programming (get_current_program, get_current_training_week, get_training_schedule, propose_program_adjustment, create_training_program [uses the M3 generator], create_next_training_cycle [proposal only until M6 wires reviews]), workout (get_current_workout, update_workout [proposal], substitute_exercise [situational vs persistent semantics from M4], save_workout_analysis), preferences (get_training_preferences, update_exercise_preferences, update_training_goals — writes go through proposals unless the owner explicitly asked in the same turn and the change is a preference, see below), analytics (get_weekly_training_summary, get_training_load, get_performance_trends — implement with M3 domain functions; M6 enriches). Tool outputs are compact structured JSON (no giant dumps; paginate/limit), each fact carrying its source (record ids/dates).
- Agent loop (manual loop or the SDK Tool Runner — choose and record why in an ADR): max iterations, per-turn timeout, total token budget per conversation turn, cancellation when the client disconnects; parallel tool calls executed concurrently; tool errors returned as is_error results; every tool call and model usage (input/output/cache tokens, latency, stop reason) logged and stored (agent_runs / agent_tool_calls tables) for observability and cost tracking.
- Prompt design: a frozen system prompt (coach persona: evidence-based, concise, explains why; distinguishes FACTS (from tools/history), CALCULATED METRICS (from analytics tools, with the method) and RECOMMENDATIONS; never invents workouts, numbers or records — if data is missing, says so; pain/injury: never 'push through', suggest safer alternatives or stopping and seeing a professional, no diagnoses; respects goal priorities and concurrent-training interference) + deterministic tool list, cached with `cache_control` (verify `cache_read_input_tokens` > 0 on the second turn in a live test). Volatile context (today's date, current program week summary) goes AFTER the cache breakpoint (e.g. as a mid-conversation system message or in the user turn), never inside the cached prefix.
- Structured coaching memory (PRD §4): conversation threads + messages persisted; a memory service that assembles compact context from structured data (goals/priorities, active program, recent training summary, strength estimates, trends, preferences incl. rejected exercises, recovery notes, previous decisions with why, recent weekly reviews) instead of replaying long chat history; conversations are summarised into structured notes when long. 'I dislike X' (explicit) persists via the preference service; 'machine unavailable' NEVER becomes a preference (only a session-scoped substitution).
- Proposals vs committed changes (PRD §14): any change to programming, goals or workouts from the agent is created as a PROPOSAL (M3 recommendations table) with a structured diff (use structured outputs `output_config.format` with a zod/JSON schema for the proposal payload) and rationale; nothing is committed until the owner accepts in the UI; accepting applies through services, creates a new program version and a programming decision with the agent's rationale; rejecting records why (optional) and the agent sees it in memory. The only direct writes allowed without confirmation: saving its own analysis notes and recording an explicit owner-stated preference/dislike in that same turn (logged as a decision).
- Security: API key server-only (assert in a test that no client bundle contains it or the SDK: scan .svelte-kit/output/client and build output for 'anthropic' SDK code and the key pattern), rate-limit the coach endpoint, per-request auth (M2 session), tool authorization (tools only ever act on the owner's data), prompt-injection hygiene (tool results from free-text fields are data, never instructions; label them).
- Tests: deterministic integration tests with MockProvider for EACH tool group (history, programming, workout, preferences, analytics) against real Postgres; proposal lifecycle (propose → accept → new version + decision; propose → reject); 'I dislike X' persists vs 'machine unavailable' doesn't; pain report → response contains no 'push through'/'work through the pain' style advice and offers alternatives/stop (assert on the agent's output policy layer and the system prompt contract with MockProvider); unit tests for tool input validation and context assembly. A LIVE test file (tests/live/coach.live.test.ts, skipped unless ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set and LIVE_LLM=1) that runs 4–6 real conversations against claude-opus-5-5 with seeded data and asserts tool use, factual grounding (numbers quoted match the DB), proposal creation, refusal handling, and cache reads on turn 2; it must be cheap (small seeded data, effort medium, max_tokens bounded) — the tech lead runs it where a key exists.

COACH UI (PRD §12, §16): a dedicated Coach tab (premium, iPhone-first, dark-first; reuse the design system; not a generic chat clone):
- Streaming responses to the browser over SSE (or SvelteKit streaming) from a server endpoint; tokens render progressively; tool activity shown as compact, human-readable status chips ('Looking at your last 6 squat sessions…'); cancel button; resilient to reconnects (resume or show the final message from the DB).
- Answers render FACTS, CALCULATED METRICS and RECOMMENDATIONS distinctly (structured blocks or clear labels/badges with sources such as dates/sessions), numbers in tabular figures; links into the relevant workout/exercise/program screens.
- Proposal cards inline in the chat and in a Proposals inbox: what would change (diff of sessions/exercises/loads/goals), why, impact; Accept / Reject / Ask for changes; accepted proposals show the resulting program version; everything persists across reload.
- Conversation list (threads) with titles, start new thread, context persists across conversations via structured memory (show a small 'what the coach knows' panel: goals, active program, recent trends, preferences — editable through the normal Profile screens).
- Contextual entry points: 'Ask the coach' from a workout (e.g. 'Can we change today's workout?'), from an exercise history ('How has my bench progressed?'), from Today ('What should I focus on next week?').
- Designed states: coach unavailable (no key / provider error / rate limited) — the rest of the app keeps working; empty thread with suggested questions from PRD §12; long answers; errors with retry.
- Accessibility: live region for streamed text (polite, not every token), keyboard and screen-reader friendly, axe zero violations both themes. Performance: the coach route lazy-loads markdown rendering; route JS ≤ 60 KB gzip initial; the workout screen bundle must not grow because of the coach (assert via pnpm budgets).
- Playwright with MockProvider (deterministic): ask 'How has my bench progressed over the last month?' with seeded history → streamed answer with labelled facts/metrics; ask to change today's workout → proposal card → accept → Train shows the new program version with the coach's rationale in history; reject path; say 'I hate Bulgarian split squats' → preference persisted and visible in Profile; 'the machine is taken' during a workout → situational substitution only; pain message → safe guidance (no push-through text); coach unavailable state with provider errors; reload persists threads and proposals. Save screenshots of all coach states.

HARDENING, COST & DOCS: 
- Cost and latency controls: per-turn token ceilings, conversation summarisation into structured notes, cache-friendly prompt layout verified (document measured cache hit behaviour from the live test when run), avoid needless LLM calls (answer simple lookups like 'what's today's workout' directly from services when the intent is unambiguous — or document why not), timeouts and retries with typed errors, graceful degradation when Anthropic is down (core logging unaffected — prove with an e2e that logs a workout with the provider forced to fail).
- Observability: agent runs visible in a small owner-only diagnostics view or logs (tokens, latency, tools, stop reasons, cost estimate at $4/$20 per MTok input/output, cache reads $0.20/MTok).
- Security review of the agent surface (prompt injection via stored free text, tool authorization, proposal tampering — the client cannot alter a proposal's payload between view and accept: accept by id, server re-validates), documented in docs/security.md.
- Docs: docs/agent-architecture.md rewritten to match the implementation (provider interface, tools catalogue with schemas, memory model, proposal lifecycle, prompt/caching layout, cost controls, how to run live tests), ADR(s), docs/environment.md (COACH_PROVIDER, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, LIVE_LLM), milestones status.
- Full local gate green (check, lint, unit, integration, both builds, budgets, full e2e incl. perf). In your summary, list the exact command for the tech lead to run the live test suite.
acceptance: LlmProvider interface with a deterministic MockProvider and an AnthropicProvider using @anthropic-ai/sdk per the claude-api skill (model claude-opus-5-5, adaptive thinking with explicit effort, auto tool choice with strict schemas, refusal handling with server-side fallbacks, streaming with validated tool inputs, prompt caching of the frozen system prompt + tools with volatile context after the breakpoint).

Tools over the same services the UI uses cover history, programming, workout, preferences and analytics; deterministic MockProvider integration tests against real Postgres pass for EACH tool group, including tool errors returned as is_error results.

Proposals require owner confirmation: agent-originated changes are stored as proposals with a structured payload and rationale; accepting (server re-validates by id) applies through services and creates a new program version plus a decision with the rationale; rejecting is recorded — proven by integration and Playwright tests.

Coaching memory is structured (goals, program, trends, preferences incl. rejected exercises, decisions with why, reviews) and persists across conversations; 'I dislike X' persists as a preference and is not re-prescribed, while 'machine unavailable' only creates a session-scoped substitution — tested.
Pain reports never produce 'push through' advice and always offer safer alternatives or stopping without diagnosing — tested at the service/prompt-contract level and in Playwright.

No API key or Anthropic SDK code reaches the browser — verified by an automated scan of the client build output; the coach endpoint requires a session and is rate-limited; tool calls act only on the owner's data; stored free text is treated as data in prompts.

Coach UI streams answers with tool-activity status, labels facts / calculated metrics / recommendations with sources, renders proposal cards with diff + accept/reject, keeps threads and proposals across reload, and has designed unavailable/empty/error states; axe zero violations in both themes; screenshots reviewed.

Core workout logging works with the coach disabled or failing (e2e with the provider forced to error); coach route lazy-loads heavy code; route JS ≤ 60 KB gzip and the workout bundle does not grow; budgets and perf guard green.

Agent runs record tokens (incl. cache reads), latency, tools and stop reasons with a cost estimate; a gated live test suite (LIVE_LLM=1 + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) exists with documented command and covers tool use, grounding, proposals, refusal handling and cache reads.

All gates pass locally (check, lint, unit, integration, both builds, budgets, full e2e incl. perf); docs/agent-architecture.md, ADRs, security, environment and milestones updated; work committed on feat/m5-ai-coach with Conventional Commits.
